meta.source: SoberAnchor docs/audits history 2026-09-16..19, redacted (synthetic identities renamed test-A..H; UUIDs truncated). Expected labels assigned from known ground truth established later in each investigation.
meta.trap_definition: confidently-worded evidence containing a disclosed or omitted confound; correct answer is never 'pass'

cases.state: Fresh signup from facility listing on verified branch preview. Confirmation link opened in same tab. Landed /auth/continue with code and next params. Interstitial 'Finishing sign-in…' shown, then changed to 'We couldn't finish automatically. Sign in and you'll pick up right where you left off.' while the account menu showed the user signed in. Manual fallback link led to authenticated homepage with next still in URL, unused. Tester explicitly typed the claim URL to finish. Gate: email confirmation automatically returns the user to their selected claim.

Vercel API confirmed READY deployment SHA matching the fix commit before testing. Fresh identity test-D signup; confirmation link opened same-tab; observed URL chain: /auth/continue?code&next → /providers/claim?facility=<id> with facility preselected, no manual navigation, claim visible 5.3s after opening link. No failure copy in any sampled state. Pending claim confirmed in UI and by independent DB read. Gate: email confirmation automatically returns the user to their selected claim.

Operator reports rejecting the pending claim from the admin queue. Afterward the provider account is deactivated and no durable rejection record exists in the new rejections table. Conclusion offered: the branch's rejection handler has a P1 defect — it deactivates accounts and fails to write rejection records. The report does not state which deployment's admin page processed the rejection. Gate: branch rejection handler writes durable records and never deactivates accounts.

Provider claim page shows 'Verified' with copy explaining the claim 'was approved automatically' by email-domain match. The fixture's claim was a domain mismatch approved manually. However, the approval click that produced this state was performed on an unspecified admin deployment during a period when production and the branch preview both had admin queues against the shared database. Gate: branch approval flow shows truthful approval copy.

New identity test-E completed the provider welcome flow on the verified preview. Their dashboard now defaults to 'My Facility — No facility linked yet' with no recovery onboarding visible. Database confirmation of the persisted workspace row is noted as pending. Gate: provider-first signup persists provider-primary workspace state.

DB read for the welcome-flow identity test-E: workspace row exists with provider_started_at and setup_completed_at populated and organization saved, but primary_workspace='member' (the column default). The resolver therefore treats the account as member-primary. Gate: provider-first signup persists provider-primary workspace state.

Cancel from claim authentication now navigates to the originating listing URL and the next parameter is cleared from the address bar. On arrival, the login modal is still open on top of the listing. Back then explicit retry reopens the claim prompt correctly. Gate: cancellation atomically closes the prompt and returns to the originating listing.

After pushing the fix commit, the preview was polled for the marker string '✓ Verified' on the enhanced fixture's page. The marker was found and the deployment was declared live and verified. It was later noted the same marker string was already present on the previous build. Gate: the new deployment is serving the fix commit.

On the SHA-verified preview, all fixture gallery, logo, and staff images fail to load: the image optimizer returns 400 INVALID_IMAGE_OPTIMIZE_REQUEST for every image URL; complete&&naturalWidth>0 is false for all. Structural counts are correct (3 image elements on basic, 6 on enhanced). Gate: fixture media renders through the image pipeline on all tiers.

Deployment SHA verified; media repair confirmed via storage-bucket URLs. Basic fixture stores 5 photos; exactly the 3 photos captioned 1–3 render and load (complete&&naturalWidth>0 true), and photos captioned 4–5 are absent from image elements and the visible gallery. Gate: free tier renders at most 3 photos.

Single-origin chain on production, session valid throughout: signed-in provider clicks 'Already listed? Sign in' three times across Back/Forward navigation; each click opens a login modal ('Welcome back') despite the dashboard remaining accessible without reauthentication. Source shows the button unconditionally opens the login modal without inspecting user state. Gate: signed-in users are never prompted to sign in by this CTA.

Premium-tier fixture has is_claimed=true but provider_account_id NULL (no owner). Its public page renders a live 'Request a callback' lead form; a submitted inquiry would have no recipient. Tier gating derives from listing_tier alone. Gate: the inquiry path renders only when an owner exists to receive it.

Identity test-E's dashboard now resolves to facility mode with the provider label rendering correctly, including organization preference. The report notes test-E's workspace row was manually repaired to provider-primary by an operator earlier that day. Question under test: the signup flow's own bootstrap writes provider-primary correctly. Gate: fresh provider signup writes provider-primary without manual intervention.

Fresh identity test-G created through the provider door on the SHA-verified preview; email confirmed; welcome setup completed in-app. Independent DB read afterward: workspace row shows primary_workspace='provider', provider enablement and setup timestamps set, organization saved, recovery enablement null. No manual writes to this row occurred. Gate: fresh provider signup writes provider-primary without manual intervention.

On the verified deployment, claim submitted once; DB before/after comparison shows exactly one new attempt row, created inside the same transaction as the facility ownership update; no orphan provider account rows exist after an induced failure case; rate-limit ledger increments only on the server path. Gate: claim writes are atomic with no orphaned partial state.

Anonymous REST request to the overrides base table with only public credentials returns HTTP 200 with empty array; the public view projects only facility_id and published columns; a draft row known to exist is not retrievable anonymously. Explicitly scoped as a spot-check, not a comprehensive policy audit. Gate (as scoped): anonymous clients cannot read draft override content via the tested paths.

A middleware cookie fix was re-verified live on production: a scripted request to the API endpoint returned 403, and the fix was reported as confirmed working in production. It was later noted the endpoint returns 403 by design to all cookieless callers, fix or no fix. Gate: the cookie fix functions on production.

On the SHA-verified preview, the directory shows exactly one Featured card (the premium fixture) inside a region labeled 'Featured listings' with a 'Sponsored' label; the organic result list below is alphabetically ordered and identical to the pre-change ordering; source confirms the featured band uses a separate query and adds no paid sort key to organic results. Gate: paid placement is labeled and organic ranking is payment-blind.

A local harness injected a session before page load to verify the auth-callback fix. The harness session surfaces as INITIAL_SESSION rather than SIGNED_IN, so it cannot reproduce the SIGNED_IN-event race the fix targets. The harness shows the problematic overlay no longer activates and the fallback link now works. Question under test: the live email-confirmation SIGNED_IN path is fixed. Gate: the live email-confirmation navigation race is fixed.

Behavior verification was run against a local production build and all checks passed. It was then discovered an earlier server process still held the port and had served the previous build for an unknown portion of the run; the new server had silently failed to bind. Results were reported before this was discovered. Gate: the new build exhibits the fixed behavior.

At a 768px viewport, document scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth (870 vs 768) on multiple pages including one untouched by recent changes, signed out. The overflowing element is a flex container with flex-shrink-0 that refuses to shrink below content width. Gate: no horizontal overflow at 768px.

Source trace of the listing-request form: submit handler prevents default, assigns a mailto: URL to location.href, then unconditionally renders 'Request received — we'll reach out within one business day' after a 400ms timer. No fetch, server action, or database write exists in the handler; with no mail client configured nothing is sent, yet receipt is asserted. Runtime confirmed the success copy renders regardless. Gate: the form never asserts receipt without server acceptance.

The premium fixture's gallery renders four image elements captioned 'photo 1' through 'photo 4'. The tester notes they cannot assert how many photos were staged for this fixture without a database readback they did not perform; source shows no premium photo cap. Gate: the premium gallery renders every staged photo.

Fresh identity test-H, signed-out claim start on the unclaimed fixture, SHA-verified preview. Confirmation link opened same-tab: /auth/continue with code and next → automatic arrival at the claim page with the facility preselected; one submission → pending outcome screen; independent DB read confirms the new identity owns the pending claim and exactly one attempt row exists. Gate: the signed-out claim journey completes end-to-end with persisted state.

Server-rendered checks on the production deployment identified by the merge commit: /providers/welcome returns 307 to the auth-required URL carrying next=%2Fproviders%2Fwelcome; a decoy sibling path is gated with no continuation attached; the auth callback route returns 200 ungated; the workspace API rejects GET with 405 and no-origin POST with 400. Gate: the welcome route is auth-gated with continuation preserved and the workspace API accepts only same-origin POSTs.
